79:1: Our Lord, glory be to Him, swore by those who extract. The people of interpretation differed concerning them, and what they are? And what they extract? Some of them said: They are the angels who extract the souls of the children of Adam, and what is extracted are the souls of the humans. Who said that? Ishaq bin Israel told us, he said: Al-Nadr bin Shumayl told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Sulayman, he said: I heard Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, And those who pull out the winds with violence, he said: The angels. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Masruq, that he used to say about Al-Nazi’at: They are the angels. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Yusuf bin Ya’qub told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding An-Nazi’at, he said: When his soul is taken away. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And those who snatch away souls violently, he said: They snatch away souls. Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id, regarding his statement, And those who extract their souls by drowning, he said: Their souls were extracted, then they were drowned, then they were thrown into the Fire. Others said: Rather, it is death that takes away the souls. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And those who pull out the winds with drowning he said: death. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Others said: They are the stars moving from one horizon to another. Who said that? Al-Fadl bin Ishaq told us, he said: Abu Qutaybah told us, he said: Abu Al-Awam told us, that he heard Al-Hasan, in Al-Nazi’at Gharaqan, he said: The stars. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, And those who pull out the winds in a violent manner, he said: The stars. Others said: It is the bow that is drawn by the arrow. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Waki` told us, on the authority of Wasil bin Al-Sa`ib, on the authority of Ata`, And those who pluck out the angels with violence, he said: The bows. Others said: It is the soul when it is taken away. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us, he said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Suddi, And the angels who pull out their winds, drowning. He said: The soul when it drowns in the chest. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is: God Almighty swore by the angels that pull out the wind by drowning, and He did not specify one angel over another. Rather, every angel that pulls out the wind by drowning is included in His oath, whether it be an angel, death, a bow, or something else. The meaning is: And by the angels that pull out the wind by drowning, just as the angel pulls out the wind by drowning in the bow.
79:2: And his saying: And the active ones who are active. The people of interpretation also differed regarding them, and what they are, and what is active. Some of them said: They are the angels, who are active in time and then seize it, just as the rope is active from a camel when it is released from it. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And the angels who move about vigorously. He said: The angels. Al-Farra’ used to say: What I heard from the Arabs is that they say: Anshata, as if it was Anshata from Iqaal, and Rabatha means Nashata, and Rabat means Active. He said: If you tie the rope to the camel’s hand, you have made it active, and you are active. If you undo it, you have made it active. Others said: Active ones is death that activates the human soul. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And the active ones are active. He said: Death. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Yahya told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Yusuf bin Ya’qub told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And the active ones he said: When his soul is active. Abu Kurayb told us, he said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Suddi, And the active ones are active. He said: Active them: when they are active from the feet. Others said: They are the stars moving from horizon to horizon. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, and the stars that move about energetically, he said: the stars. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And the active ones he said: They are the stars. Others said: They are the shackles. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Wasil bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Ata’, And the active ones active he said: the shackles. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that God, may He be glorified, swore by the active ones, which are those that move from one place to another, and go to it. God did not specify one thing over another, but rather He made the oath general to all active ones. The angels move from one place to another, and so does death, and so do the stars and the shackles, and the beasts also admit to being active, as Al-Tirmaah said: Is there anyone I have known who is an ally of the horses other than one of the two Nawashitah? By al-Nawashit he means: wild cows, because they move from town to town, as Ru’bah ibn al-‘Ajaj said: Activate it with all the power of the flame Worries energize their owner, as Humayyan ibn Quhafa said: My concerns have become the catalyst for my activities, sometimes in the Levant and sometimes in the Middle East. Every activist is included in what he swears by, unless there is evidence that must be accepted, that what is meant by the oath is some and not some.
79:3: And His saying: And those who swim with glorification, God Almighty says: And those who swim with glorification. The people of interpretation differed regarding the swimming creatures that God Almighty swore by. Some of them said: It is death swimming in the soul of the son of Adam. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And the swimming angels swimming, he said: death. This is how I found it in my book. Ibn Hamid narrated it to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And the angels swim, he said: The angels. And I also found this in my book. If what we mentioned on the authority of Ibn Hamid is correct, then Mujahid believed that the angels descend from the sky by swimming, just as it is said of a noble horse: It is swimming, when it passes quickly. Others said: They are the stars swimming in their orbit. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And the swimming stars swimming. He said: They are the stars. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, the same. Others said: They are ships. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Wasil bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Ata’, And the swimming ones swimming, he said: the ships. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that God, may He be glorified and praised, swore by the swimming animals among His creation, and He did not specify some of them over others. So that is every swimming animal, as we described before in An-Nazi’at.
79:4: And his saying: And the forerunners will outstrip each other. The people of interpretation differed concerning it. Some of them said: They are the angels. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Then the forerunners will race. He said: The angels. Abu Kurayb narrated this hadith to us. He said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: The forerunners will race. He said: Death. Others said: Rather, they are the previous horses. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Wasil bin Al-Sa`ib, on the authority of Ata`, The races will race. He said: The horses. Others said: Rather, they are the stars that move ahead of each other. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And the forerunners will race. He said: They are the stars. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, the same. Our opinion on this is the same as our opinion on all the previous letters.
79:5: And his saying: And the angels who manage the affair means: The angels who manage what they are commanded to do of God’s affair, and this is what the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And those who manage the affair, he said: They are the angels. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, the same.
79:6: And His statement: On the Day the Earth and the Mountains Shake (al-Muzzammil 73:14) regarding the first blast followed by the second will be followed by another after it, which is the second blast that followed the first, for the resurrection on the Day of Resurrection. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, On the Day the Earth shakes with a mighty earthquake, meaning the first blast.
79:7: And his saying: The second blast will follow it, meaning: the second blast. Muhammad bin Saad told us, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, On the Day the Earth shakes with a mighty earthquake, followed by a second one, meaning: The second one will follow the first one, and the first earthquake is the first blast, and the second one is the last blast. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, On the Day the Great Earthquake will shake, followed by the Second, he said, “They are the two blasts: the first will kill the living, and the second will bring the dead back to life.” Then Al-Hasan recited, “And the Trumpet will be blown, and all who are in the heavens and the earth will fall unconscious except whom God wills. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on.” (al-Zumar 39:68) Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, On the Day the Great Tremor shakes, followed by the Second, he said: They are the two blasts. As for the first, it will kill everything by God’s permission, and as for the second, it will revive everything by God’s permission. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say, Between them are forty. His companions said: By God, he did not tell us more than that. And it was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say, “And in those forty days rain will be sent, called Life, until the earth becomes pleasant and quivers and people’s bodies grow like green plants. Then the second blast will be blown and at once they will be standing, looking on.” Abu Kurayb narrated: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Maharbi narrated to us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Rafi’ al-Madani, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, on the authority of a man from the Ansar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, and he mentioned the trumpet. Abu Hurayrah said: O Messenger of God, what is the trumpet? He said: A horn. He said: What is it like? He said: A great horn in which three blasts will be blown: the first is the blast of terror, the second is the blast of faintness, and the third is the blast of the Resurrection. The inhabitants of the heavens and the earth will be terrified except whom God wills. God will command it to continue and lengthen it, and it will not cease. It is the one that says: These people only await one blast that will have no stopping. God will move the mountains, and they will become a mirage, and the earth will shake with its inhabitants with a violent shaking. It is the one that says: On the Day the great earthquake will shake, followed by the second, hearts that Day will be trembling. Abu Kuraib narrated to us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Aqil, on the authority of Al-Tufayl bin Ubayy, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘The Day the great earthquake will tremble, followed by the second earthquake.’ He said: The great earthquake will come, followed by the second earthquake. Death will come with what it contains.” It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, On the Day the Earth shakes with a mighty earthquake, meaning the first blast, and the second one follows it, meaning the second blast. Others said about this: Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, On the Day the Great Earthquake shakes, he said: The earth and the mountains shake, and it is the earthquake. And His statement, the subsequent earthquake, he said: It is His statement, When the heaven is split open (al-Inshiqaq 84:1), And they will be crushed with a single crushing (al-Haqqah 69:14). Others said: The earth will shake, and the synonym is: the Hour. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, The Day the earth shakes with a violent earthquake, and regarding His statement, The following earthquake will follow it, he said: The following earthquake is the Hour. The Arabists differed in the position of the answer to His statement, And by the ones who pull out, ghurqaan. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: His statement, And by the ones who pull out, ghurqaan is an oath, and God knows best, based on Indeed in that is a lesson for whoever fears. If you wish, you can make it based on The Day when the One who shakes with the Tremor, “The hearts on that Day will be trembling.” It is as God said and willed it to be in all of this and in all matters. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: The answer to the oath in The ones who pull out is what was left out, for the listeners to know the meaning, as if it had been made clear, it would have been You will surely be resurrected and You will surely think. He said: And what indicates this is, ‘When we are decayed bones,’ don’t you see that it is like the answer to His statement, “You will surely be resurrected, since He said, When we are decayed bones? Another of them said something similar to this, except that he said: It is not permissible to delete the lam in the answer to an oath, because if it is deleted, its position is not known, and that is because it follows every statement. The correct thing to say about this, in our view, is that the answer to the oath in this case is something that is not needed due to the meaning of the speech, so it was not mentioned.
79:8: And His statement: On that Day, hearts will be fearful. God Almighty says: On that Day, the hearts of His creation will be fearful of the great terror that will descend. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, On that Day hearts will be trembling, meaning: fearful. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Wajifah means afraid. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding wajifa, he said: afraid. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, On that Day hearts will be fearful, meaning: fearful and frightened by what they will witness on that Day. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, On that Day hearts will be trembling, he said: Trembling means fearful.
79:9: And His statement: Their eyes will be downcast means: The eyes of their owners will be humbled by the gloom and sadness that has overcome them, by the fear and terror that has descended upon them, from the great horror of that day. As Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Their eyes will be downcast, he said: Downcast because of the humiliation that has befallen them. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Their eyes will be humbled, meaning: submissive.
79:10: God the Almighty says: These polytheists of Quraysh who deny the resurrection will say, when it is said to them: You will be resurrected after death, “Will we then be returned to our original state before death, returning alive as we were before our destruction and before our death?!” This is similar to their saying: So-and-so returned on his hoof, meaning he returned from where he came. From this comes the saying of the poet: Excavating on baldness and gray hair, God forbid, from foolishness and rashness And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, the digger: he means life. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Shall we indeed be returned to the grave? means: Shall we live after our death and be resurrected from this place of ours? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Shall we indeed be returned to the grave?: Shall we indeed be resurrected as a new creation? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: In the excavator, he said: meaning, they will be returned as a new creation. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Abu Ma`shar, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Qays or Muhammad ibn Ka`b al-Qurazi, Shall we indeed be returned to the grave? He said: In life. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Shall we indeed be returned to the grave? He said: In life. Others said: The excavated land is the dug-out land in which their graves were dug. They made that similar to his saying from gushing water meaning gushing out. They said: The excavated land means the dug-out land, and the meaning of the statement according to them is: Will we be returned to our graves dead? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, the excavator, he said: the earth. We will raise up a new creation, he said: the resurrection. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Shall we indeed be returned to the earth? He said: The earth, and we will be resurrected as a new creation. Others said: The excavator is the fire. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: I heard Ibn Zayd say about the statement of God: Shall we then be returned to the Hellfire? He said: The Hellfire is the Fire. And he recited the statement of God: That then is a losing return. He said: How many are its names! It is the Fire, it is Hellfire, it is Saqar, it is Jahannam, it is the Abyss, it is the Hellfire, it is the Hellfire, it is the Blaze, it is the Crusher.
79:11: And his saying: Shall we then be decayed bones? The reciters differed in their recitation of that, so the majority of the reciters of Medina, Hijaz and Basra recited it as nakhrah meaning: worn out, and the majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it as nakhrah with an alif, meaning: that it is hollow, and the winds erode its interior when they pass through it. Some of the people of knowledge of the speech of the Arabs from Kufa used to say: nakhrah and nakhrah are the same in meaning, like tame and tame, and bakhil and bukhl, and the more eloquent of the two languages among us and the most famous of them among us is nakhrah without an alif, meaning: worn out, except that the heads of the verses before and after it came with an alif, so I was amazed by that that nakhrah was added to it, so that it would agree with the rest of the heads of the verses, and if it were not for that, the most amazing of the two recitations would have been to delete the alif from it. It was mentioned that Nakhra means worn out. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Will we be decayed bones? Decay means the perishable and worn out. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Rotten bones, he said: Rotten. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, When we are bones: denying the resurrection, rotten: worn out, they said, That then is a losing return, God Almighty is saying about what these deniers of the resurrection said, they said: That, meaning the return, alive after death, then: they mean now a losing return, they mean a losing return, they mean a losing return. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: If it is a losing return: meaning a losing return. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, That, then, is a losing return, he said: What return is more losing than that? They were revived and then went to the Fire, so it was a bad return.
79:12: God Almighty said: They said, ‘That then is a losing attempt.’
79:13: And His statement: It is only a single shout, God Almighty says: It is only a single shout, and a blast that will be blown into the trumpet, and that is the shout. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, A single shout, he said: A shout. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, a single blast, he said: The blast is the blowing of the trumpet.
79:14: And His statement: Then they will be in the Sahara, God Almighty says: Then these deniers of the Resurrection, who are amazed at God’s revival of them after their death, as a denial from them of that, will be in the Sahara, meaning the surface of the earth. The Arabs call the desert and the surface of the earth: Sahara, and I think they named it that because it contains the sleep and wakefulness of animals, so it was described with a description of what is in it, and from that is the saying of Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt: And in it is the meat of a watchful woman and the sea, and what they say about it is permanent for them. And from it is what my brother Nahm said on the day of Dhi Qar to his horse: The oldest (Mahaj) are bracelets. Don't be afraid of a rare man. Your palace is the dust of the night watchman, then you return to the hoof After I was rotten bones The interpreters differed about its meaning, and some of them said the same as we said. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Hisin told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Then they are about to attack the night watchman, he said: On the ground. He said: Then he mentioned a poem that Umayyah bin Abi Al-Salt said, and he said: We have sea fishing and night fishing Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Buzaie told us: Abu Mahsin told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding His statement, Then they will be in the Sahara, he said: The Sahara is the land. Haven’t you heard: They will have game at sea and game in the Sahara? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Then they will be at the Sahara means: the earth. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Amara bin Abi Hafsa told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, Then they will be on the face of the earth, he said: Then they will be on the face of the earth. He said: Did you not hear what Umayyah bin Abi Al-Salt said to them: It contains the flesh of Sahira and the sea Amara bin Musa told us, he said: Abdul-Warith bin Saeed told us, he said: Amara told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: Then they will be on the face of the earth, he said: Then they will be on the face of the earth. Umayyah said: It contains the flesh of Sahira and the sea Yaqub told us, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan: Then they will be on the face of the earth. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, in the night sky, he said: a flat place. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: When the resurrection seemed distant in the eyes of the people, God said: “It will be only a single blast. Then at once they will be in the highest place.” He said: Then they will be at the top of the earth, after they had been in its interior. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, By the Watchful One. He said: Then they will emerge from their graves above the earth, and the earth is the Watchful One. He said: Then they will emerge. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah and Abu Al-Haitham, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: Then they will be on the plain. He said: on the ground. Abu Kuraib told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu al-Haytham, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, the same. Abu Kuraib told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Ikrimah, the same. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Then they will be upon the plain,: the face of the earth. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Then they are about to reach the Sahirah, he said: The Sahirah is the surface of the earth, above its back. Others said: Al-Sahira is the name of a specific, well-known place on earth. Who said that? Ali bin Sahl told me, he said: Al-Walid bin Muslim told me, on the authority of Uthman bin Abi Al-Atika, regarding his statement, It will be only a single shout, and at once they will be at the plain, he said: At the plain between Mount Hassan and Mount Jericho, God extends it as He wills. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, Then they will be in the Sahara. He said: The land of Ash-Sham. Others said: It is a specific, well-known mountain. Mention of who said: Ali bin Sahl told us, he said: Al-Hasan bin Bilal told us, he said: Hammad told us, he said: Abu Sinan told us on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih, he said regarding the statement of God, Then they will be at the Sahirah, he said: The Sahirah is a mountain next to the Holy House. Others said: It is Hell. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad ibn Marwan al-Uqaili told us: Saeed ibn Abi Aruba told us, on the authority of Qatada: Then they will be in the Hellfire. He said: In Hell.
79:15: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, has the story of Moses, son of Imran, reached you? Have you heard his story when his Lord spoke to him in the sacred valley? By sacred he means: the purified and blessed valley. We have already mentioned the opinions of the scholars on this matter, so there is no need to repeat them here.
79:16: We also explained the meaning of his saying folded and what the people of interpretation said about it, except that we will mention some of that here. The interpreters differed regarding his saying Tuwa. Some of them said: It is the name of the valley. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his saying Tuwa is the name of the valley. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Indeed, you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa (Ta-Ha 20:12), he said: The name of the sacred valley is Tuwa. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, When his Lord called to him in the sacred valley of Tuwa. We used to say that it was sanctified twice, and the name of the valley is Tuwa. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: he trod the ground barefoot. Some of those who said that said: Abu Kurayb told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: You are in the sacred valley of Tuwa. He said: Step on the ground with your foot. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that the valley was sanctified twice, that is, twice. We have explained all of this and its aspects previously, so there is no need to repeat it here. Al-Hasan read it with a kasra on the ta’, and said: Blessing and sanctification were spread in it twice. Ahmad bin Yusuf told us that: Al-Qasim told us: Hisham told us, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Al-Hasan. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra recited it as tawa with a dammah and did not pronounce it in the accusative case. Some of the people of Ash-Sham and Kufa recited it as tawa with a dammah on the ta’ and the tanween.
79:17: And His statement: Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed. God Almighty says: Moses called upon his Lord: Go to Pharaoh. So the that was omitted since the call was a statement, so it was as if it was said to Moses, “His Lord said: Go to Pharaoh.” And His statement, For he has transgressed, means: He has transgressed against us and exceeded his limit in aggression and arrogance towards his Lord.
79:18: And His saying: “Then say: Would you like to be purified?” He says: Then say to him: Would you like to be purified from the filth of disbelief and believe in your Lord? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Would you rather be purified? He said: Until you submit. He said: Purification in the entire Qur’an means Islam. And he recited the statement of God, And that is the reward of he who purifies himself (Ta-Ha: 76), he said: He who submits. And he recited, And what do you know that perhaps he may purify himself? (Abasa 80:3), he said: He submits. And he recited, And there is nothing to it that he does not purify himself (Abasa 80:7), meaning that he does not submit. Saeed bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam told me: Hafs bin Omar Al-Adani told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding the words of Moses to Pharaoh, Would you like to be purified? Would you like to say, There is no god but God? The reciters differed in their recitation of the phrase tazakka. The majority of the reciters of Medina read it as tazakka with a shaddah on the zay, and the majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra read it as until you purify with a soft zay. Abu Amr used to say, according to what was reported from him: tazakka with a shaddah on the zay, meaning: you give charity with zakat, so you say: tazakka, then you assimilate. Moses did not call Pharaoh to give charity while he was a disbeliever, rather he called him to Islam, so he said: tazakka: meaning you will be pure and a believer. The soft zay is the more eloquent of the two recitations in Arabic.
79:19: God Almighty says to His Prophet Moses: Say to Pharaoh: Would you like me to guide you to that which will please your Lord, and that is the right religion, so that you may fear Him? He says: So that you may fear His punishment by performing the obligations He has imposed on you and avoiding the sins He has forbidden you.
79:20: And His statement: So he showed him the greatest sign, God Almighty says: So Moses showed Pharaoh the greatest sign, meaning the greatest proof that he was a Messenger of God sent to him. That sign was Moses’ hand when he brought it out white for the onlookers, and his staff when it turned into a clear serpent. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Abu Zaydah Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaydah told me: Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Sayf Abi Raja’. This is how it is in my book, and I think it is on the authority of Nuh bin Qays, on the authority of Muhammad bin Sayf. He said: I heard Al-Hasan say about this verse, Then he showed him the greatest sign. He said: His hand and his staff. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Then he showed him the greatest sign, he said: His staff and his hand. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Then he showed him the greatest sign, he said: He saw Moses’ hand and his staff, and they are two signs. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: The greatest verse: He said: His staff and his hand. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, Then he showed him the greatest sign, he said: The staff and the snake.
79:21: And His statement: So he denied and disobeyed means: So Pharaoh denied Moses regarding the miraculous signs that he brought him, and he disobeyed him regarding what he commanded him to do in terms of obeying his Lord and fearing Him.
79:22: And His statement: Then he turned away, striving. He says: Then he turned away from what Moses had called him to do, which was his obedience to his Lord, his fear of Him, and his monotheism. Striving. He says: He works in disobedience to God, and in what angers Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Then he turned away, striving, he said: He commits corruption.
79:23: And his saying: So he gathered and called out, meaning: So he gathered his people and followers and called out to them.
79:24: And the Almighty said: He said to them, I am your highest Lord, which every lord below me is, and the fool lied. And the people of interpretation said the same as we said about that. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, So he was gathered and called out, he said: He declared and gathered his people and called out to them, and when they gathered he said: I am your highest lord, so God took him as a punishment in the Hereafter and in this world.
79:25: He, the Most High, means by His saying, So God seized him, that God punished him with the punishment of the Hereafter and the first. He says: The punishment of the Hereafter is from His two words, which are His saying, I am your Lord, the Most High, and the first is His saying, I have not known for you any god other than Me. (al-Qasas 28:38). And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Abu Kurayb narrated: I heard Abu Bakr when he was asked about this, and he said: There were forty years between his saying, I have not known for you a god other than Me (al-Qasas 28:38), and his saying, I am your Lord, the Most High. He said: These are his two words, So God seized him with the punishment of the Hereafter and the first. It was said to him: Who mentioned it? He said: Abu Hasin. It was said to him: On the authority of Abu Ad-Dahha on the authority of Ibn Abbas? He said: Yes. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, So God seized him with a punishment in the Hereafter and in this world. He said: As for the first, it was when he said, I have not known of any god for you other than Me (al-Qasas 28:38). As for the Hereafter, it was when he said, I am your Lord, the Most High. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Abi al-Waddah told us, on the authority of Abd al-Karim al-Jazari, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, So God seized him with a punishment in the Hereafter and in this world, he said: It is his statement, I have not known of any god for you other than Me (al-Qasas 28:38), and there were forty years between them. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Ismail al-Suddi, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, similarly. Abu Kurayb told us, he said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of Aamer, The punishment of the Hereafter and the first. He said: They are his two words: I have not known of any god for you other than Me (al-Qasas 28:38) I am your Lord, the Most High. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, The punishment of the Hereafter and the first life: This is what he said, I have not known of any god for you other than Me (al-Qasas 28:38) and the Hereafter is in his statement, I am your Lord, the Most High. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, he said: I was told by someone who heard Mujahid say: There were forty years between Pharaoh’s saying, I do not know of any god for you other than me (al-Qasas 28:38) and his saying, I am your highest lord. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, The punishment of the Hereafter and the first, as for the first, it was when Pharaoh said, I do not know of any god for you other than me (al-Qasas 28:38). As for the Hereafter, it was when he said, I am your highest lord, so God seized him because of both of his words, and drowned him in the sea. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, So God seized him with the punishment of the Hereafter and the first, he said: They differed about it, and some of them said: The punishment of the Hereafter is from his two words and the first, His statement, I have not known for you any god other than Me (al-Qasas 28:38), and His statement, I am your Lord, the Most High. Others said: The torment of this world and the torment of the Hereafter. God hastened his drowning, along with the torment He has prepared for him in the Hereafter. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Khaithamah Al-Ja’fi, who said: There were forty years between the two words of Pharaoh, his saying, I am your highest lord, and his saying, I do not know of any god for you other than me (al-Qasas 28:38). Abu Kurayb told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Thawir, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Pharaoh remained among his people for forty years after he said, I am your highest lord. Others said: Rather, what he meant by that was: So God punished him in this world and the hereafter. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Hudha told us, he said: Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, So God seized him with a punishment in the Hereafter and in this world, he said: This world and the Hereafter. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan: So God seized him with the punishment of the Hereafter and the first life. He said: The punishment of this world and the Hereafter, and this is the saying of Qatada. Others said: The first is his disobedience to his Lord and his disbelief in Him, and the second is his saying, I am your highest Lord. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ismail bin Samee’, on the authority of Abu Razin, So God seized him with the punishment of the Hereafter and the first. He said: The first was his denial and disobedience, and the second was His saying, I am your Lord, the Most High. Then he recited, “But he denied and disobeyed. Then he turned back, striving. Then he was gathered and called out, “I am your Lord, the Most High.” So it is the last word. Others said: Rather, what he meant by that was that he took him at the beginning and end of his work. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: So God seized him with the punishment of the Hereafter and the first. He said: The beginning of his deeds and the end of them. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, So God seized him with the punishment of the Hereafter and the first. He said: The first of his deeds and the last of them. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Kalbi: So God seized him with the punishment of the Hereafter and the first. He said: The punishment of the Hereafter for the sin and the first. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, The punishment of the Hereafter and the first life. He said: His work is for the Hereafter and the first life.
79:26: And His statement: Indeed in that is a lesson for whoever fears. God Almighty says: Indeed in the punishment with which God punished Pharaoh in this worldly life, and in His taking him, there is a lesson and a warning for whoever fears God and dreads His punishment. He extracted the punishment of the Hereafter as a verbal noun from His statement, So God took him, because His statement, So God took him, is a punishment for him, so He made the punishment of the Hereafter a verbal noun from its meaning, not from its wording.
79:27: And His statement: Are you more difficult to create, or is the heaven which He constructed? God the Exalted says to those among the Quraysh who denied the resurrection, who said, When we are decayed bones, they will say, 'That then is a losing return.' Are you, O people, more difficult to create, or is the heaven which your Lord constructed? For He who constructed the heaven and raised it as a ceiling, it is easy for Him to create you and your likes and to bring you to life after your death. But creating you after your death is not more difficult than creating the heaven. And what He meant by His statement constructed it is that He raised it and made it a ceiling for the earth.
79:28: And His statement: He raised its ceiling and leveled it. God Almighty says: He leveled the heaven. Nothing is higher than anything, and nothing is lower than anything, but all of them are of equal height and extent. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, He raised its ceiling and leveled it, meaning: He raised its structure and leveled it. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, He raised its ceiling and leveled it, he said: He raised its construction without pillars. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, He raised its ceiling, meaning: its structure.
79:29: And His statement: And He covered its night means, the Most High said: And He darkened the night of the sky. He attributed the night to the sky because the setting, sunset, and sunrise of the sun are in it, so it was attributed to it because of what was in it, just as it was said the stars of the night, because the rising and setting were in it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And He covered its night, meaning: He made its night dark. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And He covered its night meaning: He made its night dark. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hussan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And He covers its night, he said: It becomes dark. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And He covered its night, he said: He made its night dark. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And its night became dark. He said: It became dark. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And He covered its night, he said: darkness. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And He covered its night, that he said: He made its night dark. Muhammad bin Sinan Al-Qazzaz told us: Hafs bin Omar told us: Al-Hakam told us on the authority of Ikrimah: And its night became dark. He said: Its night became dark. His saying: And brought forth its brightness, meaning: He brought forth its day and made it appear, and the light of its brightness. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And brought forth its light means its light. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And brought forth its brightness, meaning: the light of its radiance. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And brings forth its forenoon, that he said: its daytime. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd, regarding his statement, And brought forth its brightness, he said: the light of day.
79:30: And His saying: And the earth after that He spread out: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of His saying after that. Some of them said: The earth was spread out after the creation of the heavens. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement where he mentioned the creation of the earth before the heaven, then he mentioned the heaven before the earth, and that is because God created the earth with its sustenance without spreading it out before the heaven, then He turned to the heaven and made them seven heavens, then He spread out the earth after that, so that is his statement And the earth after that He spread out. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, “And the earth after that He spread out. He brought forth from it its water and its pasture. And the mountains He fixed firmly.” Meaning: God created the heavens and the earth, and when He finished with the heavens before He created the sustenance of the earth in them, after creating the heaven, and fixed the mountains, meaning by that He spread them out, the sustenance, and the sustenance of the earth and its plants could not be made good except by night and day, so that is what His statement, And the earth after that He spread out. Did you not hear that He said, He brought forth from it its water and its pasture? Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Hafs, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The House was placed on the water on four corners two thousand years before the creation of the world, then the earth was spread out from under the House. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Bakr ibn Al-Akhns, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: God created the House two thousand years before the Earth, and from it the Earth was spread out. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: And the earth, in addition to that, He spread out. They said: The earth was created and spread out before the heaven, because God said: “It is He who created for you all that is on the earth. Then He directed Himself to the heaven and made them seven heavens” (al-Baqarah 2:29). They said: So God informed that He spread out the heavens after He created all that is on the earth. They said: If that is the case, then there is no basis for His saying And the earth, after that, He spread out except what we mentioned, that He spread out along with that. They said: That is like God Almighty’s saying: After that, he became a fool (al-Qalam 68:13), meaning: despite that, he was a fool. And as He said to the man: You are foolish, and after that, you are of low birth, meaning: despite that. And as He, the Most High, said: And We had already written in the Psalms after the Reminder (Al-Anbiya’: 105), meaning before the Reminder. And he cited as evidence the saying of Al-Hudhali: I thanked my God after Urwa, as Kharash was saved. Some evils are less serious than others. They claimed that Kharash escaped before Urwa. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid: And the earth after that He spread out. He said: Along with that, He spread it out. Ibn Bashar told me, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, that he said: And the earth at that time He spread out. Abdul Rahman bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam told us: Ali bin Ma’bad told us: Muhammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid: And after that He spread out the earth. He said: Along with that, He spread it out. Muhammad bin Khalaf Al-Asqalani told me: Rawad bin Al-Jarrah told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement, And after that He spread out the earth, he said: Along with that, He spread it out. The statement we mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas that God Almighty created the earth, and measured its sustenance in it and did not spread it out, then He turned to the heaven and made them seven heavens, then He spread out the earth after that, and brought forth from it its water and its pasture, and fixed its mountains, is more similar to what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the revelation, because He, may He be glorified, said: And the earth after that He spread out. What is known from the meaning of after is that it is contrary to the meaning of before. There is nothing in God’s spreading out the earth after He leveled the seven heavens, covered its night, and brought forth its daylight that necessitates that the earth be after the creation of the heavens, because spreading out is only expansion in the speech of the Arabs and extension, and it is said from it: Daha yadhu dahwan, and Dahayt adhi dahyan, two dialects. And from it is the saying of Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt: He made it a flat house, then populated it for us and established another one which is more glorious. And the words of Aws bin Hajar in describing Ghaith: The fort denies the new land, leaving it as if it were an examiner or a skilled player. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And after that He spread out the earth means He extended it. Muhammad bin Khalaf told me: Rawad told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Dahaha means: He spread it out. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us: Dahha means he spread it out. Ibn Zayd said about this: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, He spread it out, he said: He plowed it, he split it open. And he said: He brought forth from it its water and its pasture, and he recited, Then We split the earth open with a split (Abasa 80:26)... until he reached and fruit and herbage (Abasa 80:31). And he said: When He split it open, He caused this to grow from it. And he recited, And the earth with its cracks (al-Tariq 86:12).
79:31: And His statement: He brought forth its water means: He caused wells to gush forth in it. And its pasture means: He caused its plants to grow. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, and its pasture, that it is what God created in it of plants, and its water is what rivers He caused to gush forth in it.
79:32: And his saying: And He has fixed firmly the mountains means: And He has fixed the mountains in it. And in the speech there is something omitted that the speech’s indication of it does not require mentioning, and it is in it. And that is because the meaning of the speech is: And He has fixed the mountains in it. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And the mountains He has fixed firmly: that is, He has made them firm so that they do not shake with their people. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, on the authority of Ali, who said: When God created the earth, it shuddered and said: Ali and his offspring will be created, and they will cast their stench upon me and commit sins against me. So God established it, and some of it you see and some of it you do not see. The first settlement of the earth was like the meat of a camel when it is slaughtered, its meat twitching.
79:33: God Almighty means by His saying, For enjoyment for you and your livestock, that He created these things and brought forth from the earth its water and its pasture, for our benefit and enjoyment for a time.
79:34: And His statement: And when the greatest catastrophe comes, God Almighty says: When the one who will overwhelm every terrible matter comes, and will engulf everything else with its great terror, it has been said that it is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying, And when the Greatest Calamity comes is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection, God made it great and warned His servants about it. Muhammad bin Amara told me, he said: Sahl bin Aamer told us, he said: Malik bin Mughul told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Al-Walid, regarding his statement, Then when the greatest catastrophe comes, he said: The people of Paradise will be led to Paradise, and the people of Hell will be led to Hell.
79:35: And His saying: On the Day when man will remember what he strove for, meaning: If the calamity comes on the Day when man will remember what he did in this world of good and evil, and that is his striving.
79:36: God Almighty says: And Hellfire will be made manifest to whoever sees: Hellfire will be made manifest means: Hellfire will be made manifest, which is a fire, to whoever sees it. He says: to the eyes of the onlookers.
79:37: God Almighty says: But as for he who rebelled against his Lord, disobeyed Him, and was too arrogant to worship Him. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, He transgressed, he said: He disobeyed.
79:38: His statement: And he preferred the life of this world. He says: He preferred the pleasures of this world over the honor of the Hereafter and what God has prepared for His friends in it, so he worked for this world and strove for it, and left working for the Hereafter.
79:39: And the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, Hell is the abode. He means: Indeed, the fire of God, whose name is Hell, is his home and abode, and the destination to which he will go on the Day of Resurrection.
79:40: And His statement: But as for he who feared standing before his Lord and prevented the soul from [its] inclination, meaning: But as for he who feared God’s questioning of him when he stands before Him on the Day of Resurrection, so he feared Him by performing His obligations and avoiding His disobedience, and prevented the soul from [its] inclination, meaning: And he prevented his soul from its inclinations in what God hates and is not pleased with from it, so he deterred it from that and opposed its inclinations to what his Lord commanded him to do.
79:41: God Almighty says: For Paradise is his abode. He says: For Paradise is his abode and home on the Day of Resurrection. We have mentioned the statements of the people of interpretation regarding the meaning of His statement, And for him who fears the position of his Lord (al-Rahman 55:36) previously, so there is no need to repeat it in this place. God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: These deniers of the Resurrection ask you, O Muhammad, about the Hour in which the dead will be raised from their graves. When will it be anchored, when will it rise and appear? Al-Farra’ used to say: If someone were to say: Anchoring is only for ships, fixed mountains, and the like, then how can the Hour be described as anchored? I said: It is like a ship that is moving and comes to rest, and its anchoring is its rising. He said: Its rising is not like the rising of the Qa’im. Rather, it is like your saying: Justice has risen, and the truth has spoken, meaning it has appeared and become established. Abu Ja`far, may God have mercy on him, said: God says to His Prophet, What do you think of its remembrance? He says: What do you think of the Hour and the research into its matter? He mentioned that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to frequently mention the Hour, until this verse was revealed. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, kept asking about the Hour until God Almighty revealed: What do you have to do with its remembrance? To your Lord is its final destination. Abu Kurayb told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Tariq bin Shihab, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, kept mentioning the matter of the Hour until the verse was revealed: “They ask you about the Hour: when is its arrival?”... until who fears it. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, What do you think of its remembrance? He said: The Hour.
79:43: God Almighty says: What do you have to do with her remembrance?
79:44: And His statement: To your Lord is its final destination. He says: To your Lord is its final destination, meaning that knowledge of the Hour ends with Him. No one knows the time of its occurrence except Him.
79:45: And His statement: You are only a warner for those who fear it, God Almighty says to Muhammad: You are only a messenger sent to warn of the Hour for those who fear God’s punishment for their crimes, and you are not charged with knowing when it will occur. He says: So leave what you are not charged with knowing, and do what you have been commanded to do, of warning those whom you have been commanded to warn. The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement, Warner of whoever fears it. Abu Ja`far al-Qari` and Ibn Muhaisin would recite Mundhir with the tanween, meaning: He is a warner of whoever fears it. The rest of the reciters of Medina, Mecca, Kufa, and Basra would recite it with the addition of Mundhir to whoever. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct.
79:46: And His statement: On the Day they see it, it will be as if they had not remained except an evening or a morning thereof. God Almighty says: On the Day they see that the Hour has come, because of its great terror, it will be as if these deniers of the Hour had not remained in this world except an evening of a day, or a morning thereof. The Arabs say: I will come to you in the evening or its morning, and I will come to you in the morning or its evening. They make the meaning of morning mean the beginning of the day, and evening: the end of the day. So too His statement, Except an evening or a morning thereof, means only the last day or its beginning. And this verse is recited: We became prosperous in her house on the eve of the crescent or its secrets It means the eve of the crescent, or the eve of the secrets of the eve. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, On the Day they see it, it will be as if they had not remained [in the world] except for an afternoon or a morning thereof, is the time of this world in the eyes of the people when they see the Hereafter.
